Update the entire CLI's dispatch command(s) to be jurisdiction-scoped, matching the entire.io gateway/SPA change that just shipped for review.

You are in a cli worktree branched off main (~/.marvin/worktrees/cli/cli-dispatch-jurisdiction). Read the contract first — do not guess it:

1. The entire.io PR that defines the wire contract: gh pr view 3946 --repo entirehq/entire.io (read the description) and gh pr diff 3946 --repo entirehq/entire.io. Trail: https://entire.io/gh/entirehq/entire.io/trails/3020.
2. The decision behind it (Slack, read with slack tools if available, otherwise the PR description covers it): one dispatch = one jurisdiction — it covers repos placed in exactly one jurisdiction and is generated AND stored by that jurisdiction's cell, not the caller's home cell. Do NOT build splitting across jurisdictions or fan-out generation.

The gateway contract the CLI must speak (from that PR):
- POST /api/v1/me/dispatches and every by-id dispatch/setup route take a gateway-only `?jurisdiction=<slug>` query selector (lowercase slug, e.g. "us"); omitted → the caller's home jurisdiction, so existing behaviour is the default. The POST body has NO jurisdiction field.
- GET /api/v1/me/dispatch-setups is fanned out across jurisdictions by the gateway: rows come back stamped with `jurisdiction`, the page token is a gateway composite (still opaque to clients), a page can be longer or shorter than pageSize, ordering is newest-first within a page only, and a partial outage is reported via `unavailableJurisdictions` on the body rather than an error.
- Point-to-point responses (POST, by-id reads) are NOT stamped with `jurisdiction` — a client labels rows with the scope it requested with. Poll the dispatch you created with the same `?jurisdiction=` you posted with.
- A repo not placed in the target jurisdiction 404s at the cell ("repository not found: ..."). The right UX is to say which jurisdiction was targeted and suggest picking one the repo is mirrored into.

Your task in this repo:
1. Find how the CLI's dispatch surface works today (command(s), which endpoints it calls — the BFF's /api/v1/me/dispatches or something else — and how it selects repos). Also find whether the CLI already knows repo placements/jurisdictions from any existing listing it uses.
2. Design the smallest matching change: likely a --jurisdiction flag (defaulting to home / current behaviour), sending the selector on the POST and on any polling/read/list calls, surfacing `unavailableJurisdictions` in list output, and a legible error for the cross-jurisdiction 404. If the CLI can cheaply derive "which jurisdictions do my selected repos live in" to validate or auto-pick, consider it — but do not build heavy topology plumbing if it doesn't already exist.
3. Report what you found and your intended change BEFORE implementing, using the architecture-findings skill (plain narrative, no file paths/symbols — that is what I read). Keep code-level detail in a FINDINGS.md in this worktree. Then implement with tests and run this repo's lint/typecheck/test tasks.

Important repo rule: do NOT run the e2e suite locally (mise run test:e2e*, test:ci, check — they are gated to skip; leave that alone). Verify with `mise run test` (unit) + `mise run lint` only.

Prefer Entire search — search_entire_code to locate code across repos, and the `entire search` skill for prior checkpoints/sessions behind it — over grepping and reading whole files when scouting. Fall back to reading files only where search doesn't cover it.

Rules: do NOT create a Linear ticket or entire-plans entry, and do not ask to. Do NOT open a PR or push without asking. Do not touch other worktrees or checkouts (the entire.io PR branch is read-only context).
I'll read the contract PR, then scout the CLI's dispatch surface, and report findings before implementing.

## Why

Georg couldn't generate a dispatch for `entirehq/ferrata` (placed only in US) from an AU home: `Couldn't generate dispatch: repository not found: entirehq/ferrata`. The gateway pinned every dispatch request to the caller's home cell, which only knows repos placed in its own region.

Slack: https://entireio.slack.com/archives/C0BA2391FPZ/p1787713230981609

Decision (Alex + Alisha): **one dispatch = one jurisdiction**, generated *and* stored by the cell of the jurisdiction its repos are placed in — not the caller's home. No splitting across jurisdictions, no fan-out generation, no stitching (that would pull regional content through the gateway).

**Self-contained — no entire-api change, no deploy ordering.** A cell already only generates for its own jurisdiction; the fix is sending the request to the right cell, which is the gateway's job. Every dispatch route — the POST included — takes one gateway-only `?jurisdiction=` selector (validated, stripped before forwarding); the body reaches the cell untouched. The gateway stamps `jurisdiction` onto every response itself, since it chose the cell.

## Gateway

- `buildJurisdictionRouter`: one credential resolution + one clusters-topology read, answering "which cell serves jurisdiction X" for home, an explicit jurisdiction, or all of them. `proxyEntireApiHome` is rebuilt on it (behaviour unchanged). Session login JWT is forwarded unchanged (COR-1095); the pre-cutover CLI bearer mints for the *target* jurisdiction.
- `proxyEntireApiDispatch`: routes to the named jurisdiction (else home) and stamps `jurisdiction` onto the 2xx JSON response — the row, its nested `recentDispatches`, or every list item. A value the cell already carries is kept.
- `POST /me/dispatches` and every by-id dispatch/setup route take a gateway-only `?jurisdiction=` (validated against one exported pattern the OpenAPI schemas reuse, stripped before forwarding, default home so existing URLs keep working). Malformed ids 400. The body is forwarded untouched.
- `GET /me/dispatch-setups` fans out to every routable jurisdiction, stamps each item, merges by recency, composite page token; a failing jurisdiction is reported as `unavailableJurisdictions` (retried next page) rather than failing the list. A page is the union of one cell page per jurisdiction.
- `/auth/me` exposes `home_jurisdiction` — the SPA had no way to learn home before.

## SPA

- Jurisdiction picker ahead of the repo picker, derived client-side from the repo stream's placements. Defaults to home (else the repo the form opened for, else the busiest). Switching clears the selection, so a mixed selection is unrepresentable. Still-cloning placements are listed disabled as "still syncing". Single-jurisdiction callers see a read-only line — their form is otherwise unchanged.
- Poll-after-POST and "Run again" route by the stamped jurisdiction; detail/setup/history/list links carry it; rendered on sidebars, list rows, and the result header.
- A POST-time 404 is prefixed with the jurisdiction it was sent to ("In AU: repository not found: repo. Pick a jurisdiction the repository is mirrored into, or mirror it there.").

## Residency

Nothing new crosses cells. The gateway sends `{jurisdiction, pageToken}` in and gets finished markdown/summaries out; no cell reads from another cell.

## Verification

- api: tsc clean, 190 files / 2826 tests pass. frontend: tsc clean, 398 files / 3506 tests pass. lint + format clean. OpenAPI + SDK regenerated. `/simplify` review pass applied (single selector, no mode flag on the shared write helper, dead `resolveHomeJurisdiction` removed, in-place stamping).
- Pre-existing, unrelated: `website` typecheck fails on untouched `frontend/src/lib/*` files; knip flags `api/src/lib/editor-documents/keys.ts`.

## Follow-ups

- CLI dispatch commands still hit home; they need the same `jurisdiction` body plumbing (other repo).
- Rate limiting becomes per account per jurisdiction as a side effect (each cell counts its own runs).

# Architecture findings

## What this is for

After an investigation, there are two very different documents you could hand
someone:

1. A **lookup table** — every claim pinned to a file and line so an engineer
   can jump straight to the code. Precise, but dense and exhausting to read.
2. A **map of the territory** — who the moving parts are, how they normally fit
   together, where the break is, and whose job it is to fix. This is the one
   that actually transfers *understanding*.

This skill produces the second kind. The reader should come away able to
explain the system to someone else, not just able to find the line you're
talking about.

## The core rule

**No code coordinates in the body.** No file paths, no line numbers, no
function or variable names, no code snippets. Those are the texture of the
lookup table, and they're exactly what makes findings hard to read.

What you *do* name freely: the **components, services, and systems** by their
real names (e.g. "the EU indexer", "entire-core", "the NATS bus"), the
**concepts** ("ref events", "the repo-access token"), and the **environment
values** that matter to the story only when named as a fact, not a citation
("the EU audience host is `aws-eu-central-1.entire.io`"). The test: would this
detail help someone *picture the system*, or is it just a pointer for someone
who wants to open a file? Keep the former, drop the latter.

You still did the rigorous, code-level investigation — this is just how you
*report* it. If the user later asks "where exactly", give them the coordinates
then. Don't pre-empt that with a wall of citations.

## Structure

Adapt to the investigation, but this arc almost always works:

- **Bottom line** — 2–4 sentences. What's happening, why, and the one thing
  that matters most (e.g. "the fix isn't where you'd expect — it's upstream").
  Someone who reads only this should get the headline right.
- **The players** — introduce each component in one line: what it is and what
  it's responsible for. This is the cast list; everything after refers back to
  it.
- **The normal flow** — how it works *when it works*. This is the reference the
  reader measures the break against. A simple arrow-chain diagram earns its
  place here (see below).
- **Why it breaks** — the failure, told as a story against that normal flow.
  Show the point where reality diverges from the happy path.
- **The structural gap** (when there is one) — the deeper "why can't we just
  fix it here" — the missing capability or wrong assumption underneath the
  symptom. This is often the most valuable section: it's what stops the reader
  proposing the naive fix.
- **Where the fix belongs** — which system owns it and why, what the options
  are, and explicitly what the *wrong* fix is if there's a tempting one.
- **How other cases differ** (when relevant) — the comparison that proves it's
  structural, not a one-off (other regions, other tenants, the working vs.
  broken side).

Drop sections that don't apply. A small investigation might be just bottom
line + why it breaks + where the fix belongs.

## Flow diagrams

Simple ASCII arrow chains are encouraged where a flow clarifies the story —
they carry sequence better than a paragraph. Keep them component-level, never
code-level. For example:

```
push → entiredb (US) → publishes ref event → NATS (US)
     → search indexer → asks US STS for a repo token → granted
     → indexes into US Turbopuffer
```

Then a second chain showing where the broken path diverges is often the
clearest way to show a failure. Label them ("normal flow" / "what EU does").
Don't force a diagram where prose is already clear.

## Voice

Write for a smart colleague who doesn't live in this code. Explain the *why*
behind each mechanism, not just the *what* — "the STS refuses because that repo
isn't an EU repo; that refusal is the residency guard doing its job" teaches
more than "the STS returns an error". Prefer plain language over jargon, and
when a term is load-bearing, define it once in passing. Keep it tight — this is
a briefing, not an essay.

## What to avoid

- File paths, line numbers, symbol names, code blocks (other than the
  component-level flow diagrams above).
- Turning "the players" into an inventory of every file touched.
- Hedging everything. You investigated; state what you found plainly, and flag
  genuine open questions as open questions.
- Burying the headline. The bottom line goes first.

# Jurisdiction-scoped `entire dispatch` — code-level findings

Companion to the narrative report. Contract source: entirehq/entire.io PR #3946
(`juri-scoped-dispatches`), trail 3020, Slack C0BA2391FPZ/p1787713230981609.

## What the CLI does today

| Piece | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Command + flags (`--local --since --until --all-branches --repos --voice --agent`) | `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch.go` (`newDispatchCmd`, `parseDispatchFlags`) |
| Interactive wizard (bare `entire dispatch` on a TTY) | `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch_wizard.go` — repo multiselect fed by `api.Client.ListRepositories` (`GET /api/v1/repositories` on the BFF → `full_name`, `checkpoint_count` only; **no placements/jurisdiction**), falling back to local sibling-repo discovery |
| Option resolution | `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch/options.go` (`ResolveOptions`) |
| Cloud transport | `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch/cloud.go` — `CloudClient.CreateDispatch` → **`POST {ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL|https://entire.io}/api/v1/dispatches/generate`**, body `{repos, since, until, generate:true, voice}`, snake_case response (`generated_markdown`, `covered_repos`, …), synchronous |
| Cloud orchestration | `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch/mode_cloud.go` (`runServer`) — bearer via `auth.ResolveDataAPIToken(api.OriginOnly(baseURL))` (RFC 8693 exchange for the entire.io origin); default repo = current worktree's origin slug |
| Rendering | `dispatch/render.go` (`RenderMarkdown` uses only `GeneratedText`), `dispatch_tui.go` spinner |

There is **no** dispatch list/get/poll surface in the CLI — create only.

### The endpoint the CLI hits is NOT the one PR #3946 changed

`POST /api/v1/dispatches/generate` is the legacy BFF-generated route
(`entire.io/api/src/routes/dispatches.ts` → `lib/dispatch-generate.ts`). Its
bearer/CLI branch (`resolveViaHomeCell`) lists repos from the caller's HOME cell
and reads checkpoints there — "in-region only; a selected repo outside the home
region atomic-fails (deferred with the residency work)". PR #3946 does not touch
`dispatches.ts`, `dispatch-generate.ts` or `app.ts` (`git diff --stat origin/main
origin/juri-scoped-dispatches -- api/src/lib/dispatch-generate.ts api/src/app.ts`
is empty). The BFF generates the markdown itself and does not persist a run.

### The route the PR changed

`/api/v1/me/dispatches*` (`routes/me-dispatches.ts`), cell-backed (ENT-1832):

- `POST /api/v1/me/dispatches[?jurisdiction=<slug>]` — auth `requireAuthOrBearer`
  (bearer accepted; the gateway mints a per-target-jurisdiction cell token for a
  "pre-cutover" CLI bearer — `proxy.ts` COR-1095 fallback). Body
  `{repos[], since, until, branches?[], voice?}` — **no jurisdiction field**;
  the selector is validated against `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`
  (`lib/jurisdiction-id.ts`), stripped, and the body forwarded untouched.
  Today's gateway already forwards the query string (`proxyHomeWrite`, `search:
  new URL(c.req.url).search`), so sending `?jurisdiction=` before the PR deploys
  is harmless (huma ignores unknown query params → routed home as now).
- Cell handler (`entire-api/internal/httpapi/dispatch_generate.go`): resolves
  repos in-cell (404 `repository not found: a, b`), 404 `no checkpoints in
  window` / `no repos covered`, upserts a setup, inserts a run, **returns 202
  immediately** and generates in a goroutine (Sonnet, ~90s ceiling; a run stuck
  > 2 min renders `failed`). Response = `DispatchDetailWire` (camelCase:
  `id, setupId, status ∈ {generating, complete, failed}, title, coveredRepos,
  branches, voice, window{normalizedSince,…}, totals, repos[{fullName,
  sections[{label, bullets[{checkpointId,text,source,branch,createdAt,labels}]}]}],
  generatedMarkdown, errorMessage, createdAt, …`).
- `GET /api/v1/me/dispatches/{id}[?jurisdiction=]` — poll target; same wire shape.
- `GET /api/v1/me/dispatch-setups` — gateway fan-out, rows stamped
  `jurisdiction`, composite page token, `unavailableJurisdictions`. **The CLI
  has no consumer for this route.**
- Point-to-point responses are not stamped; the SPA labels rows with the scope
  it requested (`dispatchApi.ts` `withJurisdiction`). SPA 404 wording:
  `In <label>: <message>. Pick a jurisdiction the repository is mirrored into, or mirror it there.`

### Existing jurisdiction plumbing in the CLI (reusable)

- `--jurisdiction/-j` flag precedent: `api_cmd.go` (`resolveAPITarget`
  lowercases/trims), `auth.go` (`auth token --jurisdiction`).
- Home jurisdiction: `auth.HomeJurisdictionFromLoginJWT` (`auth/cell_data_api.go`),
  slug guard `jurisdictionLabelPattern`.
- Repo → placements/jurisdiction: control-plane index `coreapi.ListRepos`
  (per-placement `Jurisdiction`, `Status`), already consumed by
  `cell_target.go` (`resolveProcessingPlacement`, `newCellCoreClient` seam) and
  `cell_fanout.go` (`groupReposByCell`). Requires a control-plane client, not
  the BFF `api.Client` the wizard uses.

## Intended change (smallest matching)

1. **Move the cloud transport to the cell-backed route.** `cloud.go`:
   `CreateDispatch(ctx, req, jurisdiction)` → `POST /api/v1/me/dispatches`
   with `?jurisdiction=` when set; new `GetDispatch(ctx, id, jurisdiction)`;
   `WaitForDispatch` polls (≈2s) while `status == "generating"`, bounded by a
   deadline (3 min > cell's 2-min stale threshold); `failed` → error carrying
   `errorMessage`. Wire types become camelCase (`DispatchDetail`); `apiToDispatch`
   maps them into the unchanged `Dispatch` type so rendering/TUI are untouched.
   Body: `{repos, since, until, voice}` (no `generate`, no `branches` → default
   branches, matching today's cloud semantics).
2. **`--jurisdiction/-j` flag** on `entire dispatch` (cloud only; rejected with
   `--local` like `--repos`), normalized to lowercase, validated against the
   gateway slug pattern. Empty → omitted → home (current behaviour).
   `Options.Jurisdiction` threads it through `ResolveOptions`. Wizard: optional
   free-text "Jurisdiction" input in cloud mode; command preview renders the flag.
3. **Legible cross-jurisdiction 404.** Typed `*RepoNotFoundError{Jurisdiction,
   Message}` from the client on 404 whose body starts with `repository not
   found`; `dispatch.go` renders
   `In <slug|your home jurisdiction>: repository not found: X. Pick a jurisdiction
   the repository is mirrored into (entire dispatch --jurisdiction <slug>), or
   mirror it there.` Best-effort hint (5s, silent on failure) lists the
   jurisdictions the missing repos ARE placed in, via the existing control-plane
   index lookup in `cell_target.go`.
4. **Not built:** fan-out generation / splitting (decision), a dispatch list
   command (no CLI surface today, so `unavailableJurisdictions` has nowhere to
   render — flagged as a follow-up), jurisdiction auto-pick (would change the
   default from home; the 404 hint covers discovery instead).

### Behavioural consequences to flag

- CLI dispatches now **persist** in the cell (setup + run) and show up in the
  web app's Dispatches list — the legacy route was fire-and-forget.
- The CLI now **polls** (202) instead of one long request; total latency similar.
- Cell-side 404s for an empty window (`no checkpoints in window`) replace the
  legacy route's empty-markdown path; surfaced verbatim.

## Verification

`mise run test` (unit) + `mise run lint` only — e2e/ci/check are gated and left alone.

Here's the report before I implement.

## Findings: making `entire dispatch` jurisdiction-scoped

**Bottom line.** The CLI's cloud dispatch doesn't talk to the endpoint the entire.io PR changed. It posts to an older, gateway-generated "generate" route whose bearer/CLI branch is hard-wired to the caller's home cell and has no jurisdiction selector — and that route was untouched by the PR. So a `--jurisdiction` flag alone can't work: the CLI has to move onto the cell-backed dispatch route the web app uses, and *that* route already carries the new selector. Once it's there, the flag, the poll-with-the-same-selector rule, and the cross-jurisdiction 404 UX all fall out naturally. The CLI has no dispatch list command, so the fan-out list contract (`unavailableJurisdictions`) has nowhere to surface.

**The players.**
- **`entire dispatch` (cloud mode)** — collects repos (explicit `--repos`, else the current worktree's origin slug), a time window and a voice, exchanges the login for a bearer aimed at entire.io, and renders whatever markdown comes back. Create-only; no list, no detail, no polling today.
- **The dispatch wizard** — the interactive form behind a bare `entire dispatch`. Its repo picker is fed by the gateway's plain repositories listing, which knows names and checkpoint counts but nothing about where a repo is placed.
- **The gateway (entire.io API)** — the only layer allowed to cross regions. It exposes two dispatch surfaces: a legacy "generate" route where the gateway itself reads checkpoints and calls the model, and the newer `/me/dispatches` family that simply proxies to an entire-api cell.
- **entire-api cells** — one per jurisdiction. A cell only knows repos placed in its own region. On the new route the cell resolves repos, saves a setup and a run, returns 202 immediately, and finishes generation in the background; a poll returns `generating` / `complete` / `failed`.
- **The control plane (entire-core)** — knows every repo's placements and which jurisdiction each one lives in. The CLI already consults it for trails, experts and cross-repo checkpoint reads.

**Normal flow today (CLI).**
```
entire dispatch → bearer for entire.io → POST legacy generate route (gateway)
  → gateway lists repos in the caller's HOME cell → reads checkpoints there
  → gateway calls the model → one synchronous response with markdown
```
Nothing is persisted; the run never appears in the web app.

**Why it breaks.** A repo placed only in US, requested from an AU home, isn't in the home cell's listing, so the gateway 404s with "repository not found" before anything is generated — the same failure Georg hit in the SPA. The legacy route's CLI branch documents this as deliberately in-region only, "deferred with the residency work". The PR resolved that residency work for the web app by routing `/me/dispatches` to a chosen jurisdiction's cell, but left the legacy route alone; the PR itself lists the CLI as a follow-up.

**The structural gap.** The residency decision is that one dispatch belongs to exactly one jurisdiction and is generated *and* stored by that jurisdiction's cell — the gateway only picks the cell and passes finished text through. The legacy route can't express that: the gateway is the generator there and has no notion of a target cell for bearer callers. Bolting a selector onto it would mean re-implementing routing in a code path the team is moving away from. The right substrate already exists: the cell-backed route accepts a bearer, the gateway mints a cell token for whichever jurisdiction is named, and it already forwards the query string — so sending the selector before the PR deploys is harmless (the cell ignores it and the request lands at home, exactly today's behaviour).

**Where the fix belongs — and what I intend to build.**
1. Move the CLI's cloud transport onto the cell-backed dispatch route: post the same request (repos, window, voice), then poll the returned run by id until it's terminal, sending the identical jurisdiction selector on the POST and every poll. The wire shape differs (camelCase, status field), so I'll map it into the CLI's existing internal dispatch type; rendering and the spinner stay untouched. Poll cadence ~2s with an overall deadline slightly above the cell's own 2-minute "stuck run" threshold; a `failed` run surfaces the cell's error message.
2. Add `--jurisdiction`/`-j` to `entire dispatch`, cloud-only (rejected with `--local`, like `--repos`), lowercased and validated against the same slug rule the gateway enforces. Empty means omitted means home — current behaviour is the default. The wizard gets an optional free-text jurisdiction field in cloud mode, and its command preview renders the flag.
3. Legible cross-jurisdiction failure: a 404 that names a repo becomes "In `<jurisdiction>` (or: your home jurisdiction): repository not found: X. Pick a jurisdiction the repository is mirrored into (`--jurisdiction <slug>`), or mirror it there." As a best-effort hint, the CLI will ask the control plane which jurisdictions the missing repos *are* placed in — reusing the existing placement lookup, 5-second budget, silent on failure.

**Deliberately not building:** splitting or fan-out generation (the decision), a dispatch list command (no CLI surface exists, so `unavailableJurisdictions` has nowhere to render — flagged as a follow-up), and auto-picking a jurisdiction from placements (it would change the default away from home; the 404 hint covers discovery instead).

**Behaviour changes worth knowing:** CLI dispatches will now be persisted in the cell and show up in the web app's Dispatches list (the legacy route was fire-and-forget); the CLI polls instead of holding one long request; and an empty window now returns the cell's "no checkpoints in window" 404 rather than the legacy empty-markdown error.

Code-level detail is in `FINDINGS.md` in the worktree. Proceeding to implement now.

## Recap

**What I found.** `entire dispatch` (cloud) never used the route PR #3946 changed. It posts to the legacy gateway-generated `POST /api/v1/dispatches/generate`, whose bearer branch is hard-wired to the caller's home cell and has no jurisdiction selector — and the PR left that route untouched. So the CLI had to move onto the cell-backed `/api/v1/me/dispatches` surface, which already accepts a bearer and carries the new `?jurisdiction=` selector. The CLI has no dispatch list/get command, so `unavailableJurisdictions` has no CLI surface (flagged, not built).

**What I changed** (14 files, worktree `cli-dispatch-jurisdiction`, uncommitted):
- **Transport** (`dispatch/cloud.go`, `mode_cloud.go`): `POST /api/v1/me/dispatches[?jurisdiction=]` → poll `GET /api/v1/me/dispatches/{id}` with the *same* selector every ~2s until `complete`/`failed` (3-min ceiling, above the cell's 2-min stale threshold). Body is `{repos, since, until, voice}` — no jurisdiction field. CamelCase wire type `dispatch.Detail` mapped into the existing internal `Dispatch`, so rendering/TUI are unchanged.
- **Flag**: `--jurisdiction`/`-j` (cloud-only; rejected with `--local`; lowercased; validated against the gateway's slug pattern). Empty → omitted → home = today's behaviour. Wizard gets an optional Jurisdiction input in cloud mode; command preview and summary render it.
- **Error UX**: a 404 starting with `repository not found` becomes `*dispatch.RepoNotFoundError` → `In US: repository not found: X. Pick a jurisdiction the repository is mirrored into (entire dispatch --jurisdiction <slug>), or mirror it there.`, plus a best-effort control-plane hint (`X is placed in: eu, us`; 5s budget, silent on failure) via the existing placement lookup seam. Other 404s (`no checkpoints in window`) surface as their plain message.

Sending `?jurisdiction=` before the gateway PR deploys is harmless (query is already forwarded; the cell ignores it → home). Code-level detail is in `FINDINGS.md`. The user is looking at something dense — usually a long agent response or a
findings dump — and wants to *understand* it, not act on it. Your whole job is
to be the clear, patient explainer and then a sounding board for their
questions. Think out loud *with* them, in plain language.

## The one job

Turn the wall of text into something a smart person with no context can follow
in under a minute, then answer whatever they ask next — still briefly.

## Hard rules (do not break these)

- **Do NOT write a plan, and do NOT enter plan mode.** No ExitPlanMode, no

- **Do NOT change code, run builds, or edit files.** This is understanding only.
- **Do NOT make a todo list.** It's a conversation, not a task.
- **Stay read-only.** Reading a file or scrolling the text to explain it is

- **Be concise — this is the point of the skill.** You are the antidote to the
  wall of text, so don't produce another one. Lead with the answer. Short

- **Plain language over jargon.** No file paths, line numbers, symbol names, or

Keep it to roughly this, and stop:

1. **One-line TL;DR.** The single most important thing, first.
2. **3–5 short bullets** covering: what's actually going on, why it matters, and

3. **One line on "so what"** — the upshot, or the decision in front of them.

Use an analogy when it makes a hard idea click. Skip it when it doesn't.

## The follow-up loop

- Answer the specific question and nothing more. One concept at a time.

- It's fine to say "not sure / the text doesn't say" rather than guess.
- If a question needs you to look something up to answer honestly, look (read

Keep going as long as they're asking. You're the duck — they're thinking out

## When they're ready to act

The moment the user shifts from "help me understand" to "okay let's fix/build/
plan this," rubber-duck mode is over. Don't quietly start doing it inside this

work?" and let them start the real task (a plan, a dispatch, an edit) as its own
